territorial_scope.description: Applies across the United States and preempts State and political subdivision laws on AI models, systems and automated decision systems in interstate commerce for five years.

evidence.quote: no State or political subdivision thereof may enforce, during the 5-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act

summary.short: Proposed federal bill that would require the President to produce a National Artificial Intelligence Action Plan within 30 days of enactment and would bar states and political subdivisions from enforcing laws regulating AI models, systems or automated decision systems in interstate commerce for five years.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill defines 'artificial intelligence', 'artificial intelligence model', 'artificial intelligence system' and 'automated decision system' (Sec. 2). Sec. 5(a) requires the President, acting through specified officials, to develop and submit to Congress a National Artificial Intelligence Action Plan within 30 days after enactment. Sec. 5(b) requires annual updates. Sec. 5(c) lists minimum contents, including identifying barriers to AI innovation, aligning federal risk management with NIST standards and frameworks, critical-infrastructure security, and measures to reduce small-business compliance burdens. Sec. 5(d) directs review of actions under Executive Orders 14110 and 14179 and suspension, revision or rescission of inconsistent actions. Sec. 6(a)(1) bars States and political subdivisions from enforcing, for five years from enactment, laws limiting, restricting or otherwise regulating AI models, systems or automated decision systems entered into interstate commerce. Sec. 6(a)(2) excludes laws whose primary purpose is to facilitate deployment or streamline procedures, certain laws imposing no substantive requirements, and provisions carrying criminal penalties. Sec. 6(b) and (c) preserve generally applicable criminal law and state procurement requirements. Sec. 7 limits federal agencies' authority to impose substantive requirements on AI beyond existing law.

relations.target_text: Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023 (Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence)
relations.note: The Action Plan must review actions taken under this Executive Order and identify any that are or may be inconsistent with the policy in section 4; agencies must suspend, revise or rescind such actions as appropriate.

evidence.quote: provide a status update on actions taken pursuant to Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025 (Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence)

relations.target_text: NIST frameworks and profiles for AI risk management and governance
relations.note: The Action Plan must align Federal risk management and governance with nationally recognized standards and guidance, including NIST frameworks and profiles, and identify additional standards work needed.

evidence.quote: including frameworks and profiles developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology

notes: Relations are limited to instruments and standards named in the bill text; no enabling act, amended or repealed law is stated. Sec. 3(8) says there is no universal legal definition of 'artificial intelligence', while Sec. 2(1) adopts the definition in section 5002 of another Act by reference; both are as written. Sec. 6(a)(1) sets the preemption moratorium at 5 years from enactment, and Sec. 4(4) describes the framework as for 'a defined period'. The text contains no legislative history, so the bill is recorded at the introduced stage only. The section_status entry is required by the schema even though relation entries are present.
